A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InsightAgent work. All 35 pages in each version, including Appendices A–I, figures, tables, equations, prompts, and detailed evaluations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original screening, summary-quality, and user-study results involving 15 systematic reviews and nine participants, plus appendix ablations and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and user-study outcomes, including the quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

M1.justification: The three-stage InsightAgent pipeline, corpus partitioning, agent navigation, memory updates, user interventions, and final synthesis remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same four prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 15 biomedical systematic reviews listed in Table 6 and the same screening, synthesis, and user-interaction tasks. No datasets, populations, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: BM25 and AutoSurvey remain the screening comparators; ChatCite and AutoSurvey remain the summary-quality baselines. ChatCite is excluded from retrieval evaluation in both versions, and Appendix B retains the same single-agent controls.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 4.2.4 retain the same title-and-abstract inputs, model configurations, top-100 baseline retrieval, expert-scoring procedure, and 50 synthesis pairs per interaction type. No experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: The multi-agent ablation in Appendix B, interaction-type analysis in Figure 4, interaction distribution in Appendix F, remdesivir case study in Appendix H, and detailed error analysis in Appendix I are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same paired t-tests in Section 4.2.3 and confidence bands in Figure 3. Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting information is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, graphical results, and appendix case evaluations match. For example, interactive GPT-4o retains 88.2% screening F1 in Table 1 and 79.7 summary-quality points in Table 2. No result entries or qualitative findings change.

T1.justification: The memory-update equation in Section 3.2 and error-prevalence definition in Appendix I are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The claims about interactive multi-agent review generation, approximately 1.5-hour completion, 79.7% of human-written quality, and improved user satisfaction remain identical in scope. Abstract copyediting does not strengthen or narrow them.

C2.justification: Interpretations of partitioning and human oversight are retained. Both versions acknowledge the same small user study, abstract-only evidence, insufficient statistical synthesis, and limited evidence weighting, including the detailed appendix qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, prompt templates, corpus reconstruction information, evaluation rubrics, questionnaires, and the code/data access statement remain unchanged. Correcting 'lanugage' and the access statement's grammar adds no technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The claimed distinction from autonomous literature-review systems is unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized copyedits improve grammar and spelling, including 'intensive labors' becoming 'labor-intensive' in the abstract and 'lanugage' becoming 'language' in Section 4.1. Appendix C slightly trims wording; section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: All seven figures and 23 tables retain their content and display structure. v2 corrects 'stematic' in Figure 1's caption, removes printed page numbers, and slightly shifts text and table positions through reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 provides small copyediting gains and removes intrusive page numbers from dense appendix displays, but preserves the explanations, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility material. These modest presentation changes, accompanied by losing printed page references, leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
